declared_non_generators: a different set of active message words
a different Hamming weight of delta_m or of the DV
a different number of near-collision blocks
a DV outside the linearized code

E1.name: step_shift_sha1
E1.scope_limit: Shift at CONSTANT LENGTH only; a different step_range length or extent is a declared_non_generator and is never absorbed.
E1.statement: A SHA-1 DV is a codeword of the linearized expansion; two DVs related by a whole-step shift of the expansion window are the same codeword read at a different offset.
E1.verification_check: expand from the shifted seed window and require exact equality over the overlapping steps, forward shifts (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) and backward shifts (1,4,8), on 64 seeded random codewords

extra.recalled_pointer_note: The Coordinator's recollection that published DV families carry a rotation index is a `recalled` pointer and was NOT treated as a reason to admit E2.

E2.failing_case: rotation b=1: the rotated pair conforms to the rotated path at only 18/80 steps (first mismatch at step 18); SHA-1's step function adds modularly and adds a FIXED constant K_t, neither of which commutes with a bit rotation
E2.name: bit_rotation_sha1
E2.statement: CONJECTURE: SHA-1's expansion and step function commute with a simultaneous left-rotation of every message word.
E2.verification_check: part 1, expansion: rot(expand(DV),b) == expand(rot(DV,b)) for all b in 0..31 on 64 seeded codewords; part 2, step function: a conforming pair is carried to a conforming pair for the rotated path. EITHER failing excludes E2.

E3.name: global_sign_flip
E3.statement: Swapping the two members of the message pair negates every signed difference; a path and its negation are the same object.
E3.verification_check: negate every signed difference and require the negated path to be conforming for the swapped pair, exactly, on 64 seeded planted paths per primitive

E4.name: signed_digit_representation_md5
E4.statement: A modular difference in Z/2^32 has many binary signed-digit representations; the canonical form is the modular difference itself.
E4.verification_check: round-trip 4096 seeded random modular differences through the signed-digit encoder/decoder; then require two DISTINCT signed representations of one modular difference to canonicalise identically and to admit the same conforming pairs on a planted path

E5.name: condition_set_normalisation
E5.scope_limit: DECIDED ON THE BOUNDED ALPHABET ONLY: 8 variables, atoms lit/eq/neq, full 2^8 enumeration. This is NOT a claim that the normal form is decidable on the full per-step 32-bit condition sets of a real characteristic; that is untested here and is a stated limit.
E5.statement: Two paths whose sufficient-condition sets have the same solution set are the same object; the canonical form is a declared normal form of the condition set.
E5.verification_check: on a bounded condition alphabet (8 boolean variables; atoms lit/eq/neq), enumerate the solution set of the condition string and of its normal form over all 2^8 assignments and require exact set equality, on 256 seeded random condition strings

E6.failing_case: step_range (0, 3): 0 of 4096 seeded draws at the second chaining value satisfied the conditions, 0 of those did not conform (VACUOUS: no draw satisfied the conditions, so the implication is empty and is NOT reported as a pass)
E6.name: block_index_reuse
E6.statement: The same per-block characteristic used at a different block index or from a different chaining value is the same object AS A PER-BLOCK CHARACTERISTIC.
E6.verification_check: part (a) the conformance predicate does not read the block index (structural: conforms() has no such parameter) and re-indexing leaves every verdict identical; part (b) at a second seeded chaining value, 4096 seeded draws per step_range in ((0, 0), (0, 3)), require condition-satisfying draws > 0 (non-vacuity) and zero condition-satisfying non-conforming draws. GATED ON THE CONJUNCTION OF BOTH RANGES, fixed before the run.

raw.quantifier_order: FOR EVERY candidate path P, THERE EXISTS a census entry C and THERE EXISTS g in <verified generators> with g(P) = C; g may depend on BOTH P and C. It is NOT claimed that a single g works for all P, and NOT claimed that the group is the full symmetry group of the difference space.
